subject: Bursting strategy & ops handoff — Artemis Analytics Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@artemisanalytics.com>, Jordan Wells <jwells@artemisanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Artemis - kickoff: dedicated pool + burst policy (initial requirements)

Hi team,

Thanks for the time yesterday, Alex + Jordan — quick follow-up from CS to loop Ops and Sales for the implementation handoff. Artemis is aiming to move inference for their GenAI assistant to a reserved GPU pool with predictable latency and the ability to burst for flash events (marketing campaigns, weekly reports). High-level asks: 

- Steady-state: 8 A100-80GB GPU capacity (in us-west1) to handle baseline traffic (~120 requests/min, median response latency target 300–500ms for 1k-token completions).
- Burst: ability to scale to ~24 GPUs for 90–120 minute spikes; target cold-to-burst readiness under 6 minutes.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive burst policy (scale-out threshold 70% GPU utilized over 2 min), conservative scale-in (hold for 15 min) to avoid oscillation.
- Regional failover: primary us-west1, fallback us-east1 within same account — customers prefer lower latency for west coast users.
- Data controls: logs retained 30 days, customer-managed KMS for keys.

I've attached an SOW draft and a regional capacity matrix for initial numbers. Ben, can you confirm contractual cadence for reserved commit vs. burst billing? Naomi, can you validate these autoscale knobs against current fleet ramp time and hot-start options (KV caching priming)?

Next steps: Ops-led tech review by 8/30, commercial confirmation by 9/1, implementation sprint kickoff week of 9/11 if both green.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@artemisanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Artemis - kickoff: dedicated pool + burst policy (initial requirements)

Monica — thanks, this is great context. Looping commercial details in-line for clarity: 

- Reserved vs. burst pricing: we should propose a 12-month reserved commit for the steady-state (8 GPUs) with an overage/burst price that is ~2.5x on-demand for additional GPUs during campaign spikes. I'll draft the pricing appendix and attach by EOD 8/30.
- SLA exception: customers requesting <6 min cold-to-burst readiness typically require warm pooling or pre-warmed nodes. Will propose a hybrid: keep a 4-GPU warm pool and allow autoscale to add up to 12 additional nodes for burst (total 24). That reduces cold-start to ~3–4 minutes for most model configs.

Operational notes for Ops (Naomi + Soojin): 
- Suggested instance mix: A100-80GB (primary) + 1-2 proxied weights on q4_HPT for lower-cost burst lanes (we can route non-latency-critical traffic there).
- KV cache priming: recommend prefix caching for top 50 conversational prompts (Artemis will provide seed prompt set).
- Fallback routing: route to us-east1 when us-west1 average tail latency >750ms for 3 consecutive mins; degrade gracefully to a smaller model variant for non-critical endpoints.

Naomi — can you confirm whether the fleet can sustain the scaling pattern without manual intervention and estimate the cold GPU boot time we should model into the SLO? Also note compliance: KMS integration is doable but procurement will need an ARO for key access.

—Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Dedicated Customers
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@artemisanalytics.com>, Jordan Wells <jwells@artemisanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Artemis - kickoff: dedicated pool + burst policy (initial requirements)

Thanks — read and confirm. Quick ops check and next actions below.

On Wed, Aug 29, 2028 at 11:05 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monica — thanks, this is great context. Looping commercial details in-line for clarity: 
> 
> - Reserved vs. burst pricing: we should propose a 12-month reserved commit for the steady-state (8 GPUs) with an overage/burst price that is ~2.5x on-demand for additional GPUs during campaign spikes. I'll draft the pricing appendix and attach by EOD 8/30.
> 
> Naomi — can you confirm whether the fleet can sustain the scaling pattern without manual intervention and estimate the cold GPU boot time we should model into the SLO?

Operational confirmation: 
- Autoscale: yes, we can automate the pattern with the runtime's continuous batching and autoscaler. Current measured cold-to-ready (full runtime + KV load) for an A100 boot + model stage is ~5:15 (avg) in our us-west pool. With a 4-GPU warm pool (Ben's suggestion) we can hit ~3:10 median for majority of requests. We'll size autoscale thresholds accordingly.
- Ramp tests: recommend a synthetic load test (weekend window) to validate 8->24 ramp within the target window and to capture tail latency. Proposed dates: 9/16 morning or 9/23 morning — operations team availability week of 9/11 for prep.
- Routing: will implement regional routing rules and health checks (tail-latency trigger >750ms x 3min). Fallback: for non-critical endpoints, auto-fall back to a quantized 4-bit variant in us-east for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Action items for Artemis: provide seed prompt list for KV priming, confirm data retention window, and sign SOW appendix for warm pool billing.

Proposed next steps / owners: 
- Ben: pricing appendix and final SOW (due 9/1).
- Monica: confirm procurement timeline and check for any procurement SLAs (due 9/1).
- Soojin & Ops: schedule ramp test date and preflight checklist (due 9/8).

I'll attach a trimmed ops playbook excerpt to the shared Drive folder with the scaling knobs we plan to use. If Artemis is comfortable, we'll plan the kickoff for week of 9/11 with a short 2-week implementation sprint.

Naomi Feldman
Senior SRE, Dedicated Services
Redwood Inference
